text: The closing condition of card I01: PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation, total PDH, activity and a tracer experiment, genotype by inhibitor; a glycaemia arm in the constitutive knockout, where glucose at P10 is already about 95 against about 130. IT7 P6 2026-10-29: decisive measurement unchanged; read PDK1, LDHA, LDHB, HK2, SLC2A1 and BNIP3 transcripts beside it in the same cells, so the replicated WWOX-deficient human neural contrast that the P3 comparison named as missing is also a second transfer test; no computational ranking selects the compound arm. (IT7 P6: the network routes added no value and the signature route was not detected, not excluded.) IT8 P3 2026-10-29, restated IT9 P4a 2026-10-30: a nanomolar pan-isoform inhibitor is added alongside dichloroacetate for the genotype-by-inhibitor arm, because dichloroacetate inhibits the recombinant human kinase isoforms only at about 0.1 to above 5 millimolar in curated database rows and a null with it alone at cell-attainable concentrations would be uninterpretable, whereas in the one document that measured both on all four isoforms the inhibitor acts at about 20 to 170 nanomolar; caveats: pan-isoform (no isoform attribution), availability for research use not stated by the sources, neuronal engagement and brain exposure not shown, second-isoform assay on a different substrate. IT9 P6 2026-10-30 (card K01): the HIF axis upstream of PDK1 is a separate, conditional experiment that can share cells and lysates with this one: HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha protein in WWOX-deficient versus corrected human neural cells first (never measured; nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions, normoxia and hypoxia), then genetic HIF1A and EPAS1 knockdown and a PX-478-class lever, with a genetic-first arm C (VHL or EGLN1 loss; a prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor only beside HIF-null and prolyl-hydroxylase-null controls, direction conditional (H-protect), not a 'mimic' of a disease direction) in knockout and corrected cells; deciding readout lactate or acidification and glucose uptake plus PGK1, ALDOA, ENO1, PFKP and PKM individually (the six readout genes and the 10-gene set are guard-scope members: a change there confirms the seed, it does not validate a lever), with network activity and viability giving the valence; the arms are conditional on the HIF-dependent shift being adaptive or harmful. IT10 P5 2026-10-31 (restated after IT10 P2.1): step 0 is run at 5 percent oxygen (physioxia) as the primary condition beside 21 and 1 percent, with a hypoxia marker and size matching in any organoid arm, an activity-silenced arm and a MYC loss-of-function arm for the rival explanations, a multielectrode network-activity readout, and two independent knockout clones with isogenic add-back. IT12 2026-10-31: (a) in vivo anchor added to step 0: HIF protein by compartment with hydroxylation, pimonidazole and lactate in perfusion-fixed or in-situ frozen P47T hippocampus and cortex, per-animal seizure count as covariate, a pre-onset age group; (b) the target panel is read gene by gene (Bhlhe40, Ddit4, Ndrg1, Egln3, Ankrd37, Adm beside Pgk1, Aldoa, Pkm, Pfkp); (c) the activity-silenced arm is decisive for the in-vivo question. Reason: the adult P47T transcripts show a broad glycolytic-enzyme shift and not the organoid's selective pattern, so three hypotheses stay apart (organoid state, activity, composition). Reopenable searches from the genetic-interaction screen GSE298081 (one unreplicated clone; association only): a second clone or re-expression screen, a neural genetic-interaction readout including LDHA, PDHA1, SLC2A1, HK2 and HIF1A, a DepMap bulk test, a ChEMBL retry (triggers NP1B1 to NP1B4).

Card F04, step E1: the isolated NMDAR current under voltage control (AMPAR and GABA-A blocked) in knockout, heterozygote and wild-type slices: amplitude, decay, NMDA:AMPA ratio, GluN2B and GluN2A shares, resting potential and input resistance; then concentration-response of d-APV and of a GluN2B-selective tool, and a use-dependent pore blocker (memantine as a translation probe, with Mg2+ and holding potential stated). Card P11: a graded bath-Mg2+ titration in the source medium with d-APV as ceiling, the composition of the recording bath, and serum and cerebrospinal-fluid Mg in the knockout mouse. The graded memantine against perampanel design of card F01 is superseded as discriminator by F04. Added in IT13 (P3b): the only human firing recovery (PMID 42397075 Fig 6) needs a wild-type + WWOX arm and a mutant WWOX arm (WW1-dead and an SDR-region mutant, with construct expression, stability and localisation shown, since a mutant is not necessarily inactive for every WWOX function) to separate recovery from a transgene effect, the organoid as the unit of testing (not ROIs or fields), at least two differentiations, an assessor blind to arm, and two independent silencers (a sodium-channel blocker and an NMDAR antagonist, with a 2-week washout) read on firing and on the CTIP2/SATB2 fraction together: read the effect against the exposure that is still active (a compound can be withdrawn, an AAV transgene keeps being expressed), and report apart an acute effect on an endpoint, a functional benefit during exposure, compensation of an impaired function, a change that persists after a compound is withdrawn, and broader recovery of WWOX functions; a reduction of firing needs controls against toxicity, cell loss and generalised suppression of activity (viability, cell number, preserved evoked responses) before it is read as a functional improvement (see the corrected bench protocol sheet). Added in IT13 (P3a): in the same neuron-deleted slices, resting potential and the M-current (Kv7) component, the isolated NMDAR current and sIPSC, littermate controls and animals as units, matched-trigger wild-type slices, a GluN2B negative allosteric modulator concentration-response beside d-APV and a Kv7 opener with reversal by an M-current blocker (prediction per reading in the design notes): a state that is secondary to illness, myelin or maturation would predict no lever. IT15 refinement: the quantity to measure is the GluN2B-sensitive share of the isolated NMDAR current (a saturating GluN2B negative modulator in the same cells). The expected current fall of a GluN2B modulator is an upper bound (incomplete inhibition, triheteromers), so burst scoring is read against an equal-current titration of a competitive glutamate-site antagonist and a low-trapping pore blocker, with a GluN2A modulator and a second, chemically unrelated GluN2B modulator as controls; a steeper-than-linear burst fall is not a discriminator alone because burst generation is threshold-like. Pore blockers show no subunit selectivity detected in recombinant-receptor data, which are not slice values.

Card E02 next measurement: lactate and LDH activity in WWOX-deficient human neural cells, the fly Ldh-alone arm and Wwox mRNA in the double line; the 42 to 500 micromolar LDH range is withdrawn as an exposure target for stiripentol (IT8 P3, below). IT7 P6 2026-10-29: read LDHA and LDHB activity separately (LDHB was the discordant gene in the P47T transfer test); no computational ranking selects the compound arm. (IT7 P6: the network routes added no value and the signature route was not detected, not excluded.) IT8 P3 2026-10-29, restated IT9 P4a 2026-10-30: the compound arm is a nanomolar human-LDHA inhibitor chosen from the curated target entries (205 qualify; 116 have no LDHB datum, 89 have a same-document LDHA and LDHB pair, of which only 2 are 30 fold or more on every pair, so selectivity over LDHB is to be established per compound); stiripentol stays only as a complex I and GABA-A comparator. Datum: enzyme data giving 7 percent inhibition at 2 millimolar and about 10 percent at 0.5 millimolar, no fitted LDH potency among its 88 curated rows (all read; one 2022 cell-level mouse-hepatocyte oxalate-output signal weighed, not decisive), a US label that names no LDH mechanism; stiripentol is not sufficiently supported as an LDH-engagement probe; the 42 to 500 micromolar figure is a secondary range.

Step 0: nuclear NRF2 and KEAP1 protein, NQO1 activity, NQO1/HMOX1/GCLM/SRXN1 transcripts, ROS reporter at baseline and after an oxidative challenge, IL-6 and IL-1beta protein after LPS with or without ATP. Step 1: the activation arms above and NFE2L2 knockdown, both genotypes, with MEA network activity and SOX2/NEUN fractions. Guards: GFAP/IBA1 counts are held-out endpoints; the six IT7 readout genes cannot decide. IT11 P2.3 additions: dimethyl and monomethyl fumarate as separate arms; NFE2L2 loss as the dependence control for every compound; off-NRF2 readouts for the fumarates (NF-kB p65 translocation, HCAR2 dependence, GAPDH activity); omaveloxolone over a concentration series spanning the low-nM NRF2-linked window and the hundreds-of-nM NF-kB/JNK/growth window with NQO1 read at each point and free exposure reported; TNF as a discriminator (NRF2-only action predicts no TNF change); an astrocyte-containing challenged arm; clone and batch recorded.

Next measurements of cards EB-ETX-01, G01 and H01: a concurrent same-day PTZ-alone control in all genotypes, an interaction test, plasma and brain exposure; for the case-level drugs, the denominators (children placed on the diet; hormonal therapy during MRI changes). IT13 (P3a): the two PTZ-alone null cohorts in the published figure differ by about the size of the ethosuximide effect, which is why a concurrent same-day control is the first requirement. Status 2026-11-05/06 (A1): the diet denominator is still not stated. At least 3 children were exposed; patients 3 and 5 have no diet entry; the narratives of patients 1-4 are not reachable. Vigabatrin MRI exposure is 2 of 2 at abstract level in a report selected for the finding, so it is not a denominator of exposed children. The same group's 64-child cohort (PMID 42735667) gives 18 of 64 with the abnormality, 9 of the 18 of genetic aetiology; the two children are probably inside it.

Graph coverage (IT11 P2.1, correcting IT10): lithium IS a seed-specific 'mimics' hit in the Q6 set (a gene-expression seed in a human system, rank 67 to 70 of 232), which IT10 missed because it read a truncated candidate list. That hit is about an expression seed and not about the lead's seizure readout: the seizure lowering also occurs in wild-type mice, and the chain rests on two network edges whose neural meaning is unverified (named in the IT11 P2.1 package). It is not support for lithium. For the neurogenic window lithium is a risk flag (Wnt activation in the same direction as the knockout MYC rise; IT11 P2.2, candidate M07); the G01 seizure lead is untouched. A development input, not an independent validation.

Graph coverage (IT11 P2.1): the graph returns d-APV only as a direct hit on the GRIN2C transcript in the Q4 direct-search arm (the earlier 'zero score' was the indirect part only); the GRIN2A, GRIN2B and GRIN2D subunits have outgoing edges but no chain reaches a Q4 seed. The hit concerns a mouse transcript, the lead's result is a bursting readout in slices: a level mismatch, not a confirmation. A development input, not an independent validation. IT13 P3b (2026-10-31): d-APV measured necessity of NMDAR activity for bursting in a neuron-deleted mouse slice (acute, reversible, no wild-type burst control); it is a different system and measure from the only human firing recovery (WWOX add-back in organoids, PMID 42397075), which has no compound arm. No compound or other pharmacological intervention has a firing readout in a human WWOX-deficient neural system (the gene add-back is the only intervention that has).

Step 0 (computational, on the deposited single-cell data if access is granted): MYC and POU5F1 difference between knockout and wild-type radial glia within G1/G0 only and within matched potency strata. Step 1 (wet lab, two independent knockout clones and corrected lines): genetic MYC lowering against a cytostatic control, with SOX2+MYC+, pH3+ and NEUN+ fractions and absolute cell counts per organoid, wild-type-plus-compound groups included; A51 and a PIN1 probe as comparison arms only; add-back before week 4 and at week 10 with MYC and CTIP2/SATB2 readouts; the SCAR12 line stratified the same way.

abstract_only; audiogenic_mouse_and_MEST; higher_concentration_than_for_absence; not_WWOX | the only WWOX link of this intervention is the ethosuximide result: the need is defined by it and T-type mediation is NOT measured; ethosuximide T-type potency (ChEMBL) is above 5 mM or 600 uM with no target against a labelled plasma range of about 283 to 708 uM; apinocaltamide is nanomolar at Cav3.1/3.2/3.3, so the documented action is coherent with the need's direction but does not itself support WWOX relevance; outside WWOX its benefit is in absence-type models, convulsive models only at higher concentration

A genotype-by-inhibitor interaction would give the first WWOX-system row for DCA on this need; the known glucose-lowering and neuropathy signals would remain as tags. A computational ranking of compounds does not change this: the IT7 P3 comparison found no added value for the network routes and an effect not detected, not excluded for the signature route, so the kind of study and the position of the need are unchanged. A null with dichloroacetate alone is not read as absence of a PDK effect. The HIF experiment (card K01) would change a different decision: a negative premise measurement drops the HIF axis for neural cells; knockdown that lowers lactate while viability or differentiation worsen marks the shift as adaptive and drops the lever; the opposite marks it harmful and gives the first WWOX-system row for the lever (F3 to F2 by rule); lactate falling with viability, network activity and differentiation unchanged or discordant leaves the valence unresolved. It does not change the position of the PDK arm of this need. IT12: nothing here moves the position; a protein-level HIF datum in P47T tissue or in human neural cells that separates activity, composition and a WWOX-specific effect would.

control_variability_comparable_to_effect; endpoint_downstream_of_need; graphical_reading; late_phase_only; no_T_type_measurement; no_drug_by_genotype_test | same paper and laboratory as lithium (PMID 32000863), one experiment, i.p., one PTZ dose, effect confined to the late phase; no wild-type or drug-by-genotype test and the wild-type arm is floor-limited, so absence of a wild-type effect is unknown, not clean; the paper reports lithium better than ethosuximide | ethosuximide T-type potency in ChEMBL is above 5 mM (screening bound) or 600 uM with target unspecified, against a labelled plasma range of about 283 to 708 uM: T-type mediation of the observed effect is not measured

Graph coverage (IT11 P2.1): the graph cannot return A51 because the name has no catalogue identity (it exists only in the paper); the lookalike BTX-A51 is not attached. A development input, not an independent validation. IT11 P2.2 restatement: the authors read the A51 result as MYC-driven impairment of differentiation (NEUN-positive up, SATB2 mildly up, CTIP2 unchanged); the arm is thin (multi-kinase compound, knockout organoids only, no wild-type-plus-compound group, supplement not available locally), so no candidate is strengthened by it; role of the MYC change stays unknown.
